Q: The ______ limit is named after a notable Nobel winning Indian Physicist. If a star’s mass crosses a certain threshold limit, it is possible that the star might turn into a black hole. This limit is named after a certain Nobel winning Indian Physicist who published a series a papers solving equations and coming to the said limit value, between 1931-35 during his journey from India to England on a boat. However, his work was heavily criticized by Arthur Eddington, a prominent Astrophysicist of the time that sparked a controversy in the physics community. Notable figures like Pauli and Bohr approved of X’s theory but never publicly supported him. His work was later proven when in 1970s astronomers observed a black hole Cygnus X which demonstrated that a star beyond the ___ limit had collapsed into something other than white dwarf.
FITB/ID X also brownie points if someone gives the actual limit.
